text:
Diego Morales: Hey team, Diego here — first week onboarding. I set up WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04) on my Windows laptop and trying to get parity with the mac dev setup. Running into a few things:

- asdf installs but `asdf install ruby 3.2.2` fails with `mkmf: gcc not found`
- my dotfiles bootstrap script chokes on symlinking .ssh on Windows paths
- direnv says `permission denied` when reading .envrc even after `direnv allow`

What do folks usually do on WSL? My quick repro steps:
```
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential curl git gnupg2 libssl-dev libreadline-dev zlib1g-dev
# installed asdf via git clone to ~/.asdf and added to ~/.profile
. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
asdf plugin-add ruby
asdf install ruby 3.2.2
```

Priya Nair (DevEx): Welcome Diego :wave: WSL is common here — a few tips we tell new hires:

- Install `build-essential` + `libssl-dev` etc (you already did, nice). The `gcc not found` means you may not have `build-essential` in the WSL distro or your shell session didn't pick up PATH after install — open a new shell after apt install.
- For Ruby we recommend installing the `libffi-dev` and `libyaml-dev` packages too:
```
sudo apt install -y libffi-dev libyaml-dev
```
- Dotfiles: avoid symlinking Windows-prefixed paths (e.g., /mnt/c/Users/...). Run the dotfiles bootstrap inside WSL root (~) so symlinks are Linux-native. If you want to share SSH keys with Windows, use the Windows OpenSSH agent and forward it into WSL or keep a separate key in `~/.ssh` inside WSL.

Ava Li: FWIW I had direnv `permission denied` because my `.envrc` file was created with CRLF line endings by a Windows editor. Convert to LF (`dos2unix .envrc`) and then `direnv allow` fixed it. Also check file mode: `chmod 600 .envrc` if it complains.

Diego Morales: Ah that CRLF thing makes sense — I edited with Notepad++ default. Converting now. Also I saw weird slow IO when bundler compiles native gems — any tips?

Priya Nair (DevEx): For heavy native builds on WSL, enable WSL2 VM memory/cpu in `~/.wslconfig` so it has enough resources. Example:
```
[wsl2]
memory=8GB
nprocessors=4
swap=2GB
```
Also disable realtime antivirus scanning on your WSL distro directories — corporate AV sometimes locks files and slows compilation.

Diego Morales: Thanks — added libs, converted .envrc, restarted shell. `asdf install ruby 3.2.2` progressed past compile errors. The dotfiles script now creates `~/.ssh/config` but my ssh-agent isn't picking the key. Any quick commands to hook Windows agent?

Ava Li: You can enable SSH agent forwarding from Windows OpenSSH into WSL with:
```
# on Windows powershell
setx WSLENV SSH_AUTH_SOCK/w
# in WSL, install socat and run a small proxy per docs
socat UNIX-LISTEN:$HOME/.ssh/agent.sock,fork TCP:localhost:0 &
# or follow https://docs.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/ssh-agent
```
But easiest is to `ssh-keygen` inside WSL and add the pub key to GH, then `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa` inside WSL.

Helpdesk Bot: If you need corporate VPN or jump-host access, file a ticket: https://internal.redwood.com/helpdesk/new-ticket (choose "WSL / dev machine").

GH Actions Bot: FYI onboarding checklist for Linux/WSL lives here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/blob/main/wsl-setup.md — includes asdf package list and recommended `apt` deps.

Priya Nair (DevEx): One last gotcha — ensure your Git `core.autocrlf` is false inside WSL to avoid CRLF toggling: `git config --global core.autocrlf false`. After that the dotfiles bootstrap should behave the same as mac/linux. Ping me if you want a quick pairing session to finalize keys and direnv rules. :thumbsup:
